analysis: Both changed files are offline CI test scripts: scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (lines 179-186 head) and scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py (patch at ~288-293). They contain no runtime provider, coordinator, crypto, attestation or key-handling code. The changes only update assertions to expect a new `route` job that picks a runner for the provider test lanes. Lane jobs now use `runs-on: fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[...]`, `needs: [changes, route]` and `timeout-minutes: 60`. For cache warming, only pull_request events may use the routed runner (`github.event_name == 'pull_request' && ...routes['warm'] || 'blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27'`). Master and dispatch warming keep the literal Blacksmith runner. That keeps release-feeding caches off the sandbox runner. The tests keep the existing negative assertions: no pull_request_target or workflow_run in the warm workflow, and no secrets, contents:write, release creation, S3 or notarytool in WARM or ACTION. The rest of the file is unchanged apart from line shifts (parity, fixture guards, native MiMo gates, composite action cache-hit bypass checks). The assertions are weakened only in how they match the runner expression, so there is no regression in the tested controls. The new `route` job, the real ci.yml and the warm workflow are not in the supplied evidence. Whether the routing step handles untrusted PR code or secrets, and whether a Darkbloom sandbox could poison caches that feed release builds, cannot be verified from these test-only diffs and should be checked where the workflow is changed. The retained threat T-041 (prefix-cache storage) is not affected.
